sections.html:
A Cheltenham sale follows the normal Pennsylvania steps, with one township requirement layered in: the seller must hand the buyer zoning and use certifications issued by the township before settlement. Cheltenham is a home-rule township in the southeast corner of Montgomery County, so the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds records the deed and the county Board of Assessment Appeals handles values.

A seller who needs to close quickly should file the township application as soon as there is a signed agreement of sale and a settlement date. The township's code says it will issue the certification statement and affidavits within 15 days of receiving the application, and no deed is registered by the township until the certifications are issued.

Cheltenham is a 9.03-square-mile inner-ring suburb that borders Philadelphia on the south and east, Abington Township and Jenkintown on the north and Springfield Township on the west. It has ten districts: Glenside, Laverock, Edge Hill, Wyncote, Cedarbrook, Chelten Hills, La Mott, Elkins Park, Melrose Park and Cheltenham Village. ZIP codes are 19012, 19027, 19038 and 19095. Housing includes rowhouses, twins and split levels, and the Cheltenham Township School District runs the public schools.

For 2020 to 2024, 62.6 percent of housing units are owner occupied and the median owner-occupied value is $384,800. Median gross rent is $1,608, median household income is $109,022, and there are 14,859 households averaging 2.47 people. Population was 37,452 in 2020 and an estimated 38,498 in July 2025. Transit is a selling point, since SEPTA Regional Rail runs through the township and bus routes start at the Cheltenham-Ogontz loop. Workers average 30.6 minutes each way.

sections.h2: What a Cheltenham seller must deliver at settlement
sections.html:
Chapter 217 of the township code, titled Property, Sale of, makes it unlawful to sell without delivering four items to the buyer at or before settlement. The township issues them on forms it provides and may inspect, though it is not required to. Call the township office at 215-887-1000 on weekdays with questions.

  • A certification of the property's zoning district from the township Zoning Officer.
  • A certification that the current use does or does not comply with township ordinances.
  • An affidavit that the street address number is displayed as Chapter 114 requires.
  • For a single-family home, an affidavit that smoke detectors meet the Fire Prevention Code.

The agreement of sale must state the zoning classification and warrant that the use complies. An owner who skips the certifications and whose use violated zoning faces a summary offense with a fine up to $600 plus costs. The fire code also requires battery-powered smoke detectors in single-family dwellings when they are sold. Fees are in the township's Chapter A300.

Cheltenham requires a rental license before an owner enters a rental agreement, and Chapter 227 requires every rental property to pass inspection against the building, property maintenance and fire codes at least once every three years. The license is a mercantile or business privilege license under the township's tax chapter.

  • Within 30 days of a transfer of ownership, the owner must give the Code Administrator written notice with the new owner's name and address.
  • The township gives at least seven days' notice before an inspection, and the owner schedules required inspections.
  • A license can be suspended or revoked for unpaid fees, uncorrected violations or refusing an inspection.
  • A summary offense under the chapter carries a fine of $50 to $1,000 per violation.

If your buyer will keep the tenants, pass along the license and inspection records. Gather the last inspection report and any correction notices before you list, because the buyer's lender and inspector will ask about the house's condition.

Cheltenham's total 2026 millage is 73.4832 mills. The pieces from the county's published list are below.

Taxing body2026 mills
Montgomery County5.462
Montgomery County Community College0.49
Cheltenham Township10.8512
School district (2026-2027)56.68
Total73.4832

The municipal bill is dated February 1 and the school bill July 1. The school share is most of the bill, so a buyer's monthly escrow depends heavily on the district.

The realty transfer tax is 2 percent, collected by the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds at recording, and Pennsylvania's share of that is 1 percent. The county also publishes a common level ratio factor, 3.36 for documents dated July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Ask the recorder for the exact total on your deed.

Permits go through the township's OpenGov portal, and since March 26, 2025 the township accepts applications only there. Permits are needed for roofing, siding, decks, kitchen and bathroom renovations, fencing, sheds and HVAC. Painting, flooring and gutter replacement do not need one, and replacement windows with no change in rough opening are exempt unless the house is in a Historic District, where added review and inspection apply.

A retaining wall that disturbs the Steep Slope Conservation District, a gradient of 15 percent or more, may need zoning relief first. Each permit carries a $4.50 state UCC charge. The township code also has chapters on sump pump standards and a vacant building registry, so owners of empty houses should look at those before listing.

1. Sign an agreement of sale and set the settlement date.
  2. File the township's application for the Chapter 217 certifications.
  3. Wait up to 15 days for the certification statement and affidavits.
  4. Install battery-powered smoke detectors if a single-family house lacks them, and make sure the street number is displayed.
  5. Hand the buyer the four items at or before settlement.

Because the township registers no deed until the certifications are issued, apply early.

sections.h2: Records to gather before you list
sections.html:
Buyers and their lenders ask for paperwork, and Cheltenham has more of it than most townships. Pull together permits for past roofing, siding, decks or HVAC work, and any correction notices from earlier inspections. If the house has a tenant, add the rental license and the last inspection report. If a building sits in the Historic District or near the Steep Slope Conservation District, ask the township what review applies before a buyer asks you.

Having these in a folder lets you answer questions in a day instead of a week, which matters when the township has up to 15 days to issue its own certifications.

sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Cheltenham
sections.html: List, sell directly or take a cash offer. A cash purchase can close sooner, but the township certifications are still required before settlement, so file the application at the start. Compare offers by what you keep after the certifications, any repairs and the transfer tax, and get each offer in writing.

faqs.q: Do I need a township certification to sell in Cheltenham?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 217 requires a zoning district certification and a use compliance certification, plus an address affidavit and, for single-family homes, a smoke detector affidavit. Apply on the township's form, and expect the answer within 15 days.

faqs.q: What happens if I skip the Cheltenham certifications?
faqs.a: The township will not register the deed, and an owner whose use violated zoning faces a summary offense with a fine up to $600 plus costs. The agreement of sale also must include the zoning and use warranty.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Cheltenham?
faqs.a: The realty transfer tax is 2 percent. The Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds collects it at recording, with the state's 1 percent included.
Cheltenham Township School District serves the township, and its 2026-2027 millage is 56.68 mills, the largest piece of the bill.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for Cheltenham building permits?
faqs.a: On the township's OpenGov portal. Paper applications ended when the portal became mandatory on March 26, 2025, and each permit carries a $4.50 UCC charge.
